nodes.title: TAXONOMY
nodes.body:
Common Name:  Sailfin molly
Scientific Name:  Poecilia latipinna

nodes.title: Classification
nodes.body:
Phylum:  Chordata
	Class:  Osteichthyes
	Order:  Atheriniformes
	Family:  Poeciliidae
Other Common Names:  Sailfin

Other:	Reference for Scientific Name (Lesueur, 1821)
	Reference for Classification (1914)

nodes.title: VALUE & STATUS
nodes.body:
Commercial:  Sailfin mollies have been used as aquarium fish (2368).
Recreational:  This molly is kept by hobbyist in home aquaria (2368).
Ecological role:  The sailfin molly is one of the most important fish in impounded wetland habitats along the Indian River Lagoon.  This species was third in overall numerical abundance, overall weight, and percent occurrence (2445; 2362).  In the trophic study conducted by Harrington and Harrington (1961), the majority of fish eaten by piscine predators in that wetland were sailfin mollies.
Indicator:  None known.

nodes.title: GEOGRAPHIC RANGE
nodes.body:
Overall:  The sailfin molly is found in coastal fresh, brackish, and salt waters from southeastern North Carolina to northwestern coast of Yucatan peninsula, Mexico (Rosen and Bailey 1963).
Within Study Area:  The sailfin molly is found throughout the Indian River Lagoon system in estuarine and freshwater wetlands (848).
Life Mode:  This livebearing euryhaline species can be found in a wide variety of habitats anywhere in the water column in groups generally feeding on vascular plants, algae, or plant detritus (2366, 2367; 2449; 2371).
Mobility and Migration: In the Indian River Lagoon, the sailfin molly utilizes the annual fall sea level rise (2446) to invade seasonally flooded wetland habitats (‘high marsh’) and produce a peak annual abundance in this area (2362).  As the water levels subside in November and December, the mollies move back into the deeper tidal creeks and marsh ponds.

nodes.title: Habitat Type
nodes.body:
The sailfin molly occurs in a variety of shallow vegetated habitats including freshwater streams and canals, mainland and barrier island wetlands (2372; 848, 993).  This species is generally associated with submerged or emergent vegetation and/or periphyton and is not commonly found in open deeper waters with little vegetational cover (2372; 848; 2371).  Mollies occur in the entire water column traveling in small to moderate sized groups (2371).
Substrate:  Sailfin mollies can be found over sand, mud, marl or sediments with large amounts of detritus in association with vegetation or periphyton (848; 2449; 2371)

nodes.title: Physical/Chemical
nodes.body:
Salinity: Sailfin mollies are euryhaline surviving in salinities from 0 to 70 ppt (2363; 2371).
Temperature: Mollies in the Indian River Lagoon can survive temperatures from 4 to at least 35 C and dissolved oxygen levels below 1 ppm (2449; 2363, Gilmore unpub. data).

nodes.title: REPRODUCTION
nodes.body:
Reproductive Mode:  The sailfin molly is a gonochoristic, iteroparous, polygamous livebearer; eggs are fertilized internally (2452; 2444)
Mating/Spawning: Spawning occurs throughout its range in the Indian River Lagoon with successful reproduction occurring from February to as late as November in the northern portions of the Lagoon (2449).  Spawning season may be longer in the southern Lagoon.  Reproduction ceases when water temperature exceeds 32-35 C (2449).  Spawning peaks occur in the spring and fall with a midsummer depression in activity (2449).  Females can produce multiple broods in a single season with interbrood intervals ranging from 21 to 68 days with an average of 34 days (2452).  Mature males range in size from 16 to 103 mm with small males depending on forced insemination while larger dominant males use aggressive behaviors to deny small males access and courtship behaviors to elicit female cooperation in mating (2451; 2454).  Females can store sperm and fertilize successive broods from one mating (2449); however single broods may be sired by multiple males (2455).
Fecundity: The number of developing embryos averages from 6.4 to 40.5 young per brood.  Number of embryos increases with size of the female (2456; 2447).

nodes.title: Length Range
nodes.body:
Egg:  Mature eggs are clear amber in color and reach a diameter of approximately 2.2 mm.  Upon reaching maturity, eggs are fertilized within the ovarian follicles (2452).  Embryogenesis continues until young are fully formed.  Length of gestation period is temperature dependent and ranges from 23 to 27 days at 26-28 C (2452).
Juvenile:  Neonates are born fully formed at lengths averaging 5.7 to 9.8 mm (2450) and may take from 50 to over 200 days to reach maturity (2453).
Adult:  Males grow very little after reaching maturity and size at maturity varies widely from 16 to over 50 mm (2457).  Age at maturity varies in the same way with small males maturing first.  Females mature generally between 22 and 37 mm (2449, 2447).  Age at maturity can range from 50 to over 200 days (2453).

nodes.title: FOOD HABITS
nodes.body: Sailfin mollies are generally herbivorous consuming vascular plants, algae, and plant detritus.  Small juveniles may consume copepods.  When mosquito larvae are present in great number, they may represent over 50% of the food volume (2366, 1982).

nodes.title: ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS
nodes.body: The sailfin molly is one of the most important fish in impounded wetland habitats along the Indian River Lagoon.  This species was third in overall numerical abundance, overall weight, and percent occurrence (2445; 2362).  In the trophic study conducted by Harrington and Harrington (1961), the majority of fish eaten by piscine predators in that wetland were sailfin mollies.

Mobility and Migration: In the Indian River Lagoon, the sailfin molly utilizes the annual fall sea level rise (2446) to invade seasonally flooded wetland habitats (‘high marsh’) and produce a peak annual abundance in this area (2362).  As the water levels subside in November and December, the mollies move back into the deeper tidal creeks and marsh ponds.

sections.heading: Habitat Type
sections.content:
The sailfin molly occurs in a variety of shallow vegetated habitats including freshwater streams and canals, mainland and barrier island wetlands (2372; 848, 993).  This species is generally associated with submerged or emergent vegetation and/or periphyton and is not commonly found in open deeper waters with little vegetational cover (2372; 848; 2371).  Mollies occur in the entire water column traveling in small to moderate sized groups (2371).
Substrate:  Sailfin mollies can be found over sand, mud, marl or sediments with large amounts of detritus in association with vegetation or periphyton (848; 2449; 2371)

sections.heading: Physical/Chemical
sections.content:
Salinity: Sailfin mollies are euryhaline surviving in salinities from 0 to 70 ppt (2363; 2371).
Temperature: Mollies in the Indian River Lagoon can survive temperatures from 4 to at least 35 C and dissolved oxygen levels below 1 ppm (2449; 2363, Gilmore unpub. data).

sections.heading: REPRODUCTION
sections.content:
Reproductive Mode:  The sailfin molly is a gonochoristic, iteroparous, polygamous livebearer; eggs are fertilized internally (2452; 2444)
Mating/Spawning: Spawning occurs throughout its range in the Indian River Lagoon with successful reproduction occurring from February to as late as November in the northern portions of the Lagoon (2449).  Spawning season may be longer in the southern Lagoon.  Reproduction ceases when water temperature exceeds 32-35 C (2449).  Spawning peaks occur in the spring and fall with a midsummer depression in activity (2449).  Females can produce multiple broods in a single season with interbrood intervals ranging from 21 to 68 days with an average of 34 days (2452).  Mature males range in size from 16 to 103 mm with small males depending on forced insemination while larger dominant males use aggressive behaviors to deny small males access and courtship behaviors to elicit female cooperation in mating (2451; 2454).  Females can store sperm and fertilize successive broods from one mating (2449); however single broods may be sired by multiple males (2455).
Fecundity: The number of developing embryos averages from 6.4 to 40.5 young per brood.  Number of embryos increases with size of the female (2456; 2447).

sections.heading: Length Range
sections.content:
Egg:  Mature eggs are clear amber in color and reach a diameter of approximately 2.2 mm.  Upon reaching maturity, eggs are fertilized within the ovarian follicles (2452).  Embryogenesis continues until young are fully formed.  Length of gestation period is temperature dependent and ranges from 23 to 27 days at 26-28 C (2452).
Juvenile:  Neonates are born fully formed at lengths averaging 5.7 to 9.8 mm (2450) and may take from 50 to over 200 days to reach maturity (2453).
Adult:  Males grow very little after reaching maturity and size at maturity varies widely from 16 to over 50 mm (2457).  Age at maturity varies in the same way with small males maturing first.  Females mature generally between 22 and 37 mm (2449, 2447).  Age at maturity can range from 50 to over 200 days (2453).

sections.heading: FOOD HABITS
sections.content: Sailfin mollies are generally herbivorous consuming vascular plants, algae, and plant detritus.  Small juveniles may consume copepods.  When mosquito larvae are present in great number, they may represent over 50% of the food volume (2366, 1982).

sections.heading: ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS
sections.content: The sailfin molly is one of the most important fish in impounded wetland habitats along the Indian River Lagoon.  This species was third in overall numerical abundance, overall weight, and percent occurrence (2445; 2362).  In the trophic study conducted by Harrington and Harrington (1961), the majority of fish eaten by piscine predators in that wetland were sailfin mollies.
